text: New daily thread dissecting the biggest crypto hacks: the DAO, Ronin, Wormhole, Bybit and more. Not how much was stolen, but the one line of code or the one key that failed. 52 heists, one a day.

card.title: Anatomy of a crypto heist
card.foot: Not how much was taken, but what failed.

text: The DAO paid out before updating its books. Ronin fell to one phished employee. Wormhole skipped one check and minted 120,000 wETH from nothing. I'm dissecting one crypto hack like this every day in a new thread.

card.title: What really failed
card.sub: One crypto hack explained every day.

text: How do you steal $1.5B from a cold wallet without ever stealing its keys? Bybit found out in February 2025. That's one of 52 crypto heists I'm taking apart, one a day, in a new thread.

card.q: How do you rob a cold wallet without its keys?

text: From The DAO in 2016 to Ronin, Wormhole and Bybit: I started a daily thread retracing a decade of crypto heists, explained technically but readable without being a dev.

card.title: A decade of crypto heists
card.sub: Explained technically, readable without being a dev.

text: People think crypto hacks mean someone broke the cryptography. Almost never: it's a forgotten check, a leaked key, a fake job offer, a tampered screen. My new daily thread shows what really failed, case by case.
